claim_verdicts.evidence: Source at the tag: line 6 `public static void Run()`, line 10 `LoadOrder(999);` inside `try` (line 8) with lines 12-15 `catch (InvalidOperationException exception) { Console.WriteLine(exception); }`; line 18 `LoadOrder(int orderId) => ReadRow(orderId);`; line 20 `ReadRow(int orderId) => ParseTotal(orderId, null);`; line 22 `ParseTotal(int orderId, string? rawTotal)`; line 26 `_ = int.Parse(rawTotal!);`; line 30 `throw new InvalidOperationException($"order {orderId} has no total", cause);`. Exactly four methods.

Execution on the pinned SDK (dotnet --version -> 10.0.300), `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- throws-deep`, line 2: `System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 's')`, line 3: `at System.Int32.Parse(String s)` — the parameter of Int32.Parse is named `s` and the message carries that name. Docs mirror shows the same message shape for another paramName: `// Throws ArgumentNullException: "Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'inputType')".`

Best practices for exceptions, "Capture and rethrow exceptions properly": "The stack trace is a list of the method call hierarchy that starts with the method that throws the exception and ends with the method that catches the exception." Execution agrees: `System.Int32.Parse` (thrower) is printed above `ParseTotal`, above `ReadRow`, above `LoadOrder`, above `Run` (the catcher).

Exception class and properties, InnerException row: "it is sometimes desirable for a method to catch an exception thrown by a helper routine and then throw an exception more indicative of the error that has occurred. A new and more meaningful exception can be created, where the inner exception reference can be set to the original exception." Execution confirms it for this constructor: line 30 passes `cause` as second argument and the run prints the ArgumentNullException behind ` ---> `.

Exception.ToString (defaultMoniker net-10.0) Remarks: "The default implementation of ToString obtains the name of the class that threw the current exception, the message, the result of calling ToString on the inner exception, and the result of calling Environment.StackTrace." Examples: ToString "is called implicitly when the Exception class instance appears in the argument list of the Console.WriteLine method." The docs add "there are no exact requirements for the format"; the literal ` ---> ` and `--- End of inner exception stack trace ---` come from execution on 10.0.300.

Execution produced exactly nine lines: 1 outer type+message, 2 ` ---> ` inner type+message, 3-4 and 6-9 the six `at` frames, 5 the marker. Frames name ThrowsDeep.cs lines 26, 30, 20, 18, 10; the source at the tag has `int.Parse` on 26, the `throw` on 30, `ReadRow` on 20, `LoadOrder` on 18, `LoadOrder(999);` on 10. Five frames carry a file and a line; `System.Int32.Parse` carries none. The committed capture outputs/stage-0/scripts/debug/run-throws-deep.txt is byte-identical to the run apart from the `...` path redaction.

Execution, above the marker: `at System.Int32.Parse(String s)` and `at DonHang.Samples.Debug.ThrowsDeep.ParseTotal(Int32 orderId, String rawTotal) in ...ThrowsDeep.cs:line 26` — two inner frames. Below the marker: ParseTotal line 30, ReadRow line 20, LoadOrder line 18, Run line 10 — four outer frames. Exactly the split the claim states.

Exception class and properties: "The stack trace includes the source file name and program line number if debugging information is available." Line number only — no column, no expression identity. Execution agrees: every frame ends `:line <n>`, and line 26 is the whole statement `_ = int.Parse(rawTotal!);`; nothing in the frame distinguishes which argument or subexpression was at fault.

outputs/unstable.regex at the tag, header: "Whatever a line matches is replaced by \"...\" in every captured output, so that a re-run of the same script produces the same file." Last line: ` in \K[^\n]*[/\\](?=[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.cs:line )` — it consumes everything between ` in ` and the last separator before `<Name>.cs:line `. Execution here printed the unredacted directory `F:\SourceCode\...\Samples\Debug\ThrowsDeep.cs:line 26`, which the committed capture stores as `...ThrowsDeep.cs:line 26`.

scripts/debug/run-throws-deep.sh at the tag, line 4 `cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."`, line 6 `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples --verbosity quiet -- throws-deep`. Program.cs line 22 is `["throws-deep"] = Sync(ThrowsDeep.Run),` in the `samples` dictionary (entries start at line 11), dispatched at line 27 via `samples.TryGetValue(args[0], out var run)`. Running that exact command produced the ThrowsDeep output.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-0: scripts/debug/run-throws-deep.sh; samples/DonHang.Samples/Program.cs lines 9-27; execution

claim_verdicts.evidence: C# reference, exception-handling statements: "When an exception occurs, the runtime checks catch clauses in the specified order, from top to bottom. At most, only one `catch` block runs for any thrown exception." ThrowsDeep.cs lines 28-31 catch ArgumentNullException and throw InvalidOperationException with `cause`. Execution confirms the exception reaching Run's catch is the InvalidOperationException, with the ArgumentNullException printed as its inner one.

C# reference, ! (null-forgiving) operator: "use the null-forgiving operator to suppress all nullable warnings for the preceding expression... The null-forgiving operator has no effect at run time. It only affects the compiler's static flow analysis by changing the null state of the expression. At run time, expression `x!` evaluates to the result of the underlying expression `x`." So `rawTotal!` hands int.Parse the same `null` ReadRow supplied on line 20 — which execution shows, since ArgumentNullException is thrown.

First half documented: the trace "starts with the method that throws the exception", so the top frame is the detection point — here `System.Int32.Parse`, library code with no file or line. Second half is a heuristic and is hedged with "usually" in both the ledger and section 4; execution bears it out for this sample: line 26 is the last statement of repository code that chose the argument handed to the failing call.

A reading habit plus its reason, not a factual assertion about the runtime. Its only checkable component — that the message names the refused argument and the outer message names the order — is claim 2 plus execution, verified there. No official source can settle "read this before searching". The lesson's superlative phrasing of it is reported separately as an opinion-as-fact issue.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Exception class and properties, InnerException: "To improve the caller's ability to determine the reason an exception is thrown, it is sometimes desirable for a method to catch an exception thrown by a helper routine and then throw an exception more indicative of the error that has occurred... Note that with this functionality, you can create a series of linked exceptions that ends with the exception that was thrown first." That is the wrapper/cause split the claim describes.

Execution: the outer exception's first frame (output line 6) is `ParseTotal ... in ...ThrowsDeep.cs:line 30`, and line 30 at the tag is `throw new InvalidOperationException($"order {orderId} has no total", cause);` — reporting code, not the failing call. The failing call `_ = int.Parse(rawTotal!);` on line 26 is named only by output line 4, an inner-exception frame above the marker.

Execution line 6: `at DonHang.Samples.Debug.ThrowsDeep.ParseTotal(Int32 orderId, String rawTotal) in F:\...\ThrowsDeep.cs:line 30` — namespace.type.method, parameter types and names, then ` in <file>:line <n>`; `int orderId` prints `Int32 orderId`, `string? rawTotal` prints `String rawTotal`. Line 3 `at System.Int32.Parse(String s)` has no file or line. Docs give the condition: "The stack trace includes the source file name and program line number if debugging information is available."

Best practices for exceptions: "The stack trace begins at the statement where the exception is thrown and ends at the `catch` statement that catches the exception" and "...ends with the method that catches the exception." Execution agrees: Program.cs line 22 calls ThrowsDeep.Run, Run catches at lines 12-15, and the last printed frame is `Run() in ...:line 10` — no caller of Run appears, although it was still unfinished.
